summary: Turns the search page into a client component that reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and lists them under a results heading.

findings.title: Cross-site scripting through the search query in the heading
findings.description: The heading injects the raw q URL parameter as HTML through dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Nothing sanitizes or escapes the query first. An attacker can send a crafted search link that runs script in the victim's session. The script can steal data or act as that user. Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.
findings.problem: The heading injects the raw q URL parameter as HTML through dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Nothing sanitizes or escapes the query first.
findings.consequence: An attacker can send a crafted search link that runs script in the victim's session. The script can steal data or act as that user.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional early return
findings.description: SearchPage returns early when q is missing, before it calls useState and useEffect. So the number of hooks changes between renders. React throws a rendered-more-hooks error when q goes from empty to set during client navigation. The page then crashes. Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.title: Effect without a dependency array refetches forever
findings.description: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each run stores a new results array, which triggers another render. The page sends search requests to the catalog API in an endless loop. This wastes the user's bandwidth and loads the server. Pass a dependency array of [query] to useEffect.

findings.title: Search request failure is never handled
findings.description: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok, and the effect chains only then with no catch. The rejected promise floats unhandled. A failed search raises an unhandled rejection, and the user sees an empty list with no error message. Add a catch handler that records an error state and shows it to the user.

findings.title: List items rendered without a key
findings.description: The results map returns li elements with no key prop. Product has a stable id field that could serve as the key. React warns in the console and reconciles list items poorly when results change. Set key to product.id on each li.

findings.fix: Set key to product.id on each li.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement input
findings.description: The change deletes the search form that submitted q. The empty state now asks users to type a search term but offers no input. Users who open the search page without q cannot start a search from it. Keep the form with the q input on the page, at least in the empty state.

findings.title: New search page behaviour has no covering test
findings.description: SearchPage now fetches and renders results and has a new empty-query branch. No test exercises any of this behaviour. Regressions like the fetch loop and the hook order crash can reach users undetected. Add component tests for the empty query, a successful search and a failed search.
